references.text: Laying hands on the head of the sacrificial animal is a recurring ritual in the law of offerings, symbolizing identification with the sacrifice.
The same ritual act of laying hands on the head of the sacrificial animal before slaughter.
Parallel text regarding laying hands for the sin offering for the priest.
Nearly identical wording concerning laying hands and slaughtering at the place of burnt offering for the sin offering.
Parallel text about laying hands and slaughtering the sin offering (female lamb) at the place of burnt offering.
Specifies the location for slaughtering the burnt offering on the north side of the altar, the same place where the sin offering was to be slaughtered.
Confirms that the sin offering is to be slaughtered in the same place as the burnt offering, before the Lord's presence.
Aaron places both hands on the head of the goat and confesses the people's sins, showing the transfer of sin to the sacrificial animal.
The New Testament explains that under the law almost everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
